customer.name: Alpine Outfitters
currentProblems: The implementation team is new to Saviynt terminology
Business users do not yet understand identities, accounts, and applications
The access request catalog has not been introduced
Managers need a basic certification walkthrough
The team needs a simple go-live readiness checklist
goals: Understand core identity governance building blocks
Distinguish identities, accounts, applications, roles, and entitlements
Explain basic joiner provisioning
Introduce requestable access and manager approvals
Complete a beginner-friendly certification and go-live review

summary: Alpine Outfitters is beginning its first Saviynt implementation. The organization is not facing a crisis; the goal is to help a new implementation team understand the platform's core concepts before they move into more complex customer scenarios.
introduction: You are starting your first week as a junior Saviynt consultant. Your mentor asks you to help Alpine Outfitters with introductory configuration and governance tasks. The engagement teaches the basics of authoritative sources, identities, accounts, provisioning, requests, approvals, certifications, and go-live readiness.

phases.title: Identity Governance Basics
phases.scenario: Alpine Outfitters is preparing for its first Saviynt design workshop. The project team wants to understand which systems provide identity data and which systems Saviynt will govern.

events.title: First Design Workshop
events.message: Your mentor asks you to help the team identify the source of employee data and the applications that will be governed first.

questions.prompt: Which system is the authoritative source for employee identities at Alpine Outfitters?
correctAnswers: Workday
questions.explanation: Workday is the authoritative source because it owns the employee record used to create and update identities in Saviynt.

questions.prompt: Which systems are examples of applications Saviynt can govern?
choices: A spreadsheet used only for meeting notes
correctAnswers: Active Directory
Salesforce
Microsoft Entra ID
Point of Sale System
questions.explanation: Saviynt can govern business and technical systems that contain accounts or access. A private meeting-notes spreadsheet is not a governed application in this scenario.

questions.prompt: Arrange the basic employee lifecycle events in their normal order.
elements: Joiner
Mover
Leaver
correctOrder: Joiner
Mover
Leaver
questions.explanation: A typical employee lifecycle begins when the person joins, continues when they move roles or departments, and ends when they leave.

successEffects.message: The team understands the basic Saviynt implementation vocabulary.
Clear ownership of employee identity data reduces confusion during design.

failureEffects.message: The team remains confused about which system owns employee identity data.
Unclear application ownership creates avoidable design risk.

phases.title: Users, Identities, and Accounts
phases.scenario: The HR team creates a new employee in Workday. The employee appears in Saviynt, but no target-system accounts exist yet. The business team asks what this means.
learningObjectives: Explain account correlation at a basic level

events.title: New Hire Walkthrough
events.message: A store associate has been added to Workday. Your mentor asks you to explain what should happen next in simple terms.

questions.prompt: A new employee appears in Saviynt from Workday, but does not yet have an Active Directory account. What currently exists?
choices: An identity exists, but the Active Directory account does not
An Active Directory account exists, but no identity exists
The employee has already completed certification
A Segregation of Duties violation has occurred
correctAnswers: An identity exists, but the Active Directory account does not
questions.explanation: The identity represents the person. The Active Directory account is separate and can be provisioned later.

questions.prompt: What is an orphan account?
choices: An account that is not linked to a known identity
A user who forgot their password
correctAnswers: An account that is not linked to a known identity
questions.explanation: An orphan account is an account that Saviynt cannot confidently associate with a governed identity.

questions.prompt: Arrange the basic account-correlation flow.
choices: Compare account attributes to identity attributes
Review accounts that could not be matched
correctAnswers: Import accounts from the application
Compare account attributes to identity attributes
Link matching accounts to identities
Review accounts that could not be matched
questions.explanation: Correlation starts with account import, compares account data to identity data, links confident matches, and leaves unmatched accounts for review.

successEffects.message: The team correctly identifies and reviews unmatched accounts.
Business users understand the difference between people and accounts.

failureEffects.message: Unmatched accounts are not reviewed because the team misunderstands correlation.
Stakeholders confuse identities with application accounts.

phases.title: Provisioning and Access Requests
phases.scenario: Alpine Outfitters wants new employees to receive basic access automatically and allow employees to request extra access when needed.
learningObjectives: Introduce Technical Rules and birthright access

events.title: First Access Catalog Review
events.message: The team reviews which access should be automatic for new employees and which access should be requested through the catalog.

questions.prompt: Arrange the basic joiner provisioning timeline.
choices: Target-system accounts or access are created
correctAnswers: Workday creates the employee record
Saviynt imports the identity
Saviynt evaluates basic access rules
Provisioning tasks are created
Target-system accounts or access are created
questions.explanation: Joiner provisioning normally starts in the authoritative source, flows into Saviynt, evaluates rules, creates tasks, and updates target applications.

questions.prompt: What does it mean to make an application requestable?
choices: Users can request access to it through the access request catalog
The application is deleted from Saviynt
The application no longer needs an owner
All users automatically receive every entitlement
correctAnswers: Users can request access to it through the access request catalog
questions.explanation: A requestable application or entitlement can be selected by eligible users during an access request.

questions.prompt: Which items may commonly be requested through Saviynt?
correctAnswers: Applications
Roles
Entitlements
questions.explanation: Saviynt access requests commonly involve applications, roles, and entitlements, not unrelated physical or branding items.

successEffects.message: The team understands the basic provisioning sequence and avoids common setup confusion.
Employees now understand how to request access through the catalog.
Requestable access is tied to clear business ownership.

failureEffects.message: Provisioning confusion causes avoidable setup errors.
Employees do not understand how requestable access should work.

phases.title: Approvals and Certifications
phases.scenario: Managers will approve common access requests and later review whether employees still need their assigned access.

events.title: Manager Governance Training
events.message: Store managers need a simple explanation of what they approve during requests and review during certifications.

questions.prompt: Who commonly approves a manager-based access request?
correctAnswers: The user's manager
questions.explanation: In a manager-based approval, the user's manager is the expected approver.

questions.prompt: Why are access certifications performed?
choices: To verify users still need their access
correctAnswers: To verify users still need their access
questions.explanation: Certifications are periodic reviews used to confirm whether access remains appropriate.

questions.prompt: Arrange the simple certification process.
elements: Certification is launched
Reviewer examines user access
Reviewer approves or revokes access
Revoked access is remediated
correctOrder: Certification is launched
Reviewer examines user access
Reviewer approves or revokes access
Revoked access is remediated
questions.explanation: A certification starts with launch, moves to reviewer decisions, and finishes when revoke decisions are remediated.

successEffects.message: Managers understand how to complete a basic access review.
The organization can explain why access reviews matter.
Managers feel prepared instead of overwhelmed.

failureEffects.message: Managers are unsure how to complete review tasks.
The business cannot clearly explain why access reviews are performed.

phases.title: Beginner Go-Live Readiness
phases.scenario: The project team asks whether Alpine Outfitters is ready for a limited pilot launch with a small group of employees and managers.
learningObjectives: Connect identity governance benefits to business value

events.title: Pilot Launch Decision
events.message: The project sponsor asks for a plain-language summary of what Saviynt will help the company control.

questions.prompt: Which items should be checked before a beginner pilot launch?
choices: A small set of applications is configured
Basic request and approval flow works
Managers know how to complete simple reviews
Every possible application in the company is fully onboarded
correctAnswers: Authoritative identity import works
A small set of applications is configured
Basic request and approval flow works
Managers know how to complete simple reviews
questions.explanation: A beginner pilot should prove the core flow with limited scope. It does not require every application in the company to be onboarded.

questions.prompt: Which are common benefits of identity governance?
correctAnswers: Better access visibility
More consistent approvals
Improved compliance evidence
Automated or tracked provisioning
questions.explanation: Identity governance improves visibility, approval consistency, compliance evidence, and provisioning control. It does not make the network faster.

questions.prompt: The sponsor asks, 'How do we know Saviynt is providing value?' Choose the best response.
choices: It helps automate identity lifecycle management, improve access governance, and provide evidence that access is approved, reviewed, and removed when needed.
It guarantees no one will ever request the wrong access.
It removes the need for managers and application owners.
correctAnswers: It helps automate identity lifecycle management, improve access governance, and provide evidence that access is approved, reviewed, and removed when needed.
questions.explanation: The strongest answer connects Saviynt to lifecycle management, governance, evidence, approvals, reviews, and access removal without overpromising.

successEffects.message: The sponsor approves a small pilot launch.
The team can explain the controls Saviynt will provide.
Application and access ownership are clearer before pilot launch.

failureEffects.message: The sponsor delays the pilot because the team cannot explain the value clearly.
Readiness gaps remain unresolved before pilot launch.

successConclusion.title: Tutorial Engagement Complete
successConclusion.message: Alpine Outfitters completes a successful beginner pilot. The team now understands the core Saviynt concepts: authoritative sources, identities, accounts, applications, provisioning, access requests, approvals, certifications, remediation, and basic go-live readiness.
successConclusion.outcome: You are ready to move from beginner training into medium-difficulty consulting engagements.

failureConclusion.title: Pilot Launch Needs More Preparation
failureConclusion.message: Alpine Outfitters is not yet ready for a pilot launch. The gaps are basic and fixable: the team needs more practice with identity sources, account correlation, requestability, approvals, certifications, and go-live evidence.
failureConclusion.outcome: Review the beginner concepts and repeat the engagement before moving into more complex customer scenarios.

title: Saviynt Go-Live

visuals.alt: Financial institution preparing for an identity governance launch

customer.name: Northwind Bank
currentProblems: Orphan accounts remain unresolved across governed applications
Salesforce provisioning is inconsistent for new joiners
Manager-based approval routing is unreliable
SAP segregation-of-duties conflicts remain unresolved
Go-live and regulatory-audit readiness evidence is incomplete

summary: Northwind Bank is approaching production go-live for its Saviynt implementation while also preparing for a regulatory audit. Core integrations are largely operational, but unresolved identity, provisioning, approval-routing, and segregation-of-duties issues could delay the launch and weaken the bank's audit position.
introduction: You have joined Northwind Bank during the final stage of its Saviynt implementation. Your responsibility is to investigate the remaining governance and provisioning issues, stabilize the environment, and determine whether the organization is ready for production go-live and regulatory review.

days.title: Discovery and Architecture Review
days.scenario: You meet with the identity team and review the current Saviynt architecture. Workday is the authoritative source. Active Directory and SAP are mostly stable, but Salesforce provisioning is inconsistent and the regulatory audit begins shortly after the planned go-live.
learningObjectives: Identify authoritative sources and governed applications
Understand the current application and provisioning architecture

questions.prompt: Which areas should you review first to understand Salesforce provisioning failures?
correctAnswers: Salesforce endpoint configuration
Salesforce connector mappings
Technical Rules assigning Salesforce access
Provisioning task history
questions.explanation: Salesforce-specific failures should be investigated through assignment logic, endpoint configuration, connector mappings, and provisioning evidence.

questions.prompt: Arrange the investigation for joiners missing Salesforce access.
questions.explanation: Start upstream with identity import and lifecycle processing, then move into access assignment, provisioning, and target-system validation.
correctAnswers: Verify Workday identity import
Confirm Joiner lifecycle processing
Review Technical Rules
Inspect Salesforce provisioning logs
Validate Salesforce account creation

questions.prompt: Which findings should be treated as go-live blockers rather than post-launch improvements?
choices: High-risk Salesforce provisioning failures remain unresolved
SAP SoD conflicts have no owner or mitigation
Manager approvals route to inactive or incorrect reviewers
A dashboard uses an outdated color palette
correctAnswers: Terminated users retain active accounts
High-risk Salesforce provisioning failures remain unresolved
SAP SoD conflicts have no owner or mitigation
Manager approvals route to inactive or incorrect reviewers
questions.explanation: Go-live blockers are failures that can create unauthorized access, prevent required business access, invalidate approvals, or leave material compliance risks unmanaged.

days.title: Identity Correlation and Orphan-Account Cleanup
days.scenario: The identity team identifies hundreds of orphan accounts across Active Directory, Salesforce, and SAP. Some belong to contractors, some use legacy naming conventions, and others may belong to terminated workers.
learningObjectives: Prioritize remediation based on risk and ownership

questions.prompt: Which evidence should you collect before deciding how to remediate an orphan account?
correctAnswers: Account status and last activity
Application and entitlement risk
Possible identity matches
Account owner or business custodian
Creation and request history
questions.explanation: An orphan account should be classified using identity matching, ownership, activity, risk, and historical evidence before it is correlated, disabled, or removed.

questions.prompt: Arrange the investigation and remediation process for orphan accounts.
choices: Review account attributes and possible identity matches
Validate ownership, activity, and business purpose
Reconcile and verify the final state
correctAnswers: Identify orphan and uncorrelated accounts
Review account attributes and possible identity matches
Validate ownership, activity, and business purpose
Correct correlation or approve remediation
Disable or remove unauthorized accounts
Reconcile and verify the final state
questions.explanation: Orphan-account cleanup should distinguish valid correlation problems from unauthorized accounts and verify every corrective action in the target system.

questions.prompt: An active privileged SAP account has no correlated identity and no confirmed business owner. What is the strongest immediate response?
choices: Escalate it as high risk, restrict or disable it through the approved process, and investigate ownership
Correlate it to the first user with a similar name
Leave it active until the annual certification
Delete the account immediately without collecting evidence
correctAnswers: Escalate it as high risk, restrict or disable it through the approved process, and investigate ownership
questions.explanation: An unattributed privileged account is a high-risk condition. It should be contained through an approved process while ownership and legitimacy are investigated.

days.title: Salesforce Provisioning Stabilization
days.scenario: Workday imports and Joiner processing are completing, but some new employees receive Active Directory access without Salesforce accounts or required permission sets. Other Salesforce tasks remain in a failed or pending state.
learningObjectives: Trace the full Joiner provisioning lifecycle
Troubleshoot Salesforce endpoint and mapping failures
Define evidence required for production readiness

questions.prompt: Arrange the expected lifecycle for a joiner receiving Salesforce access.
choices: Saviynt imports and updates the identity
Joiner processing and Technical Rules evaluate access
A Salesforce provisioning task is generated
The connector creates the account and assigns access
correctAnswers: Workday creates the employee record
Saviynt imports and updates the identity
Joiner processing and Technical Rules evaluate access
A Salesforce provisioning task is generated
The connector creates the account and assigns access
Reconciliation confirms the target state
questions.explanation: The complete lifecycle runs from authoritative identity creation through access calculation, provisioning, and target-state confirmation.

questions.prompt: Which conditions could cause Salesforce account creation to succeed while required permission sets are missing?
choices: Technical Rule conditions assign the account but not the required access
A provisioning action for permission sets fails
The connector account lacks permission to assign the access
The certification campaign has not yet launched
correctAnswers: Incomplete entitlement mappings
Technical Rule conditions assign the account but not the required access
A provisioning action for permission sets fails
The connector account lacks permission to assign the access
questions.explanation: Partial provisioning commonly results from assignment logic, mapping, connector permission, or entitlement-action failures rather than certification configuration.

questions.prompt: Which evidence should be produced before Salesforce provisioning is declared ready for go-live?
choices: Successful Joiner tests for representative user populations
Successful account creation, modification, and removal tests
Failure handling, retry, and escalation results
A screenshot of the Salesforce login page
correctAnswers: Successful Joiner tests for representative user populations
Successful account creation, modification, and removal tests
Permission-set assignment and removal validation
Failure handling, retry, and escalation results
Reconciliation confirming the target-system state
questions.explanation: Production readiness requires evidence across positive and negative scenarios, lifecycle changes, access removal, operational failure handling, and reconciliation.

days.title: Approval Routing and SAP SoD Remediation
days.scenario: A recent reorganization changed hundreds of manager relationships. Some access requests now route to former managers, while several SAP requests create unresolved segregation-of-duties conflicts.

questions.prompt: Arrange the investigation for requests routing to the wrong manager.
choices: Verify the manager relationship in Workday
Confirm the manager attribute was imported into Saviynt
Review the affected identity in the Identity Repository
Confirm new requests reach the correct approver
correctAnswers: Verify the manager relationship in Workday
Confirm the manager attribute was imported into Saviynt
Review the affected identity in the Identity Repository
Inspect workflow manager-resolution logic
Run a controlled request-routing test
Confirm new requests reach the correct approver
questions.explanation: Approval-routing troubleshooting should follow the manager value from the authoritative source through import, storage, workflow resolution, and controlled validation.

questions.prompt: Which controls should be applied when an SAP access request creates an SoD conflict?
choices: Identify the conflicting business functions and entitlements
Route the exception to accountable risk or application owners
Define compensating controls and an exception review date
Record the final approval or rejection decision
Automatically approve the request when the manager approves
correctAnswers: Identify the conflicting business functions and entitlements
Require documented business justification
Route the exception to accountable risk or application owners
Define compensating controls and an exception review date
Record the final approval or rejection decision
questions.explanation: SoD exceptions require clear conflict visibility, accountable approval, documented justification, mitigation, and periodic review rather than manager approval alone.

questions.prompt: A user temporarily requires conflicting SAP access for quarter-end processing. What is the strongest governance approach?
choices: Approve a documented, mitigated, time-bound exception with an accountable owner and expiration date
Grant the access permanently because the request is urgent
Remove the SoD rule until quarter-end is complete
Allow the user's manager to approve without recording an exception
correctAnswers: Approve a documented, mitigated, time-bound exception with an accountable owner and expiration date
questions.explanation: Temporary conflicting access should be governed as a documented, owned, mitigated, and expiring exception.

days.title: Go-Live and Regulatory Readiness Decision
days.scenario: The go-live steering committee meets tomorrow. Executives need a clear recommendation supported by evidence covering identity data, provisioning, approvals, SoD, orphan-account remediation, and operational monitoring.
learningObjectives: Communicate remaining risk and go-live recommendations

questions.prompt: Which evidence should be included in the final go-live and regulatory-readiness package?
choices: Salesforce provisioning and reconciliation test evidence
SAP SoD violations, mitigations, and exception ownership
Operational monitoring and failed-task escalation procedures
The development team's preferred code editor
correctAnswers: Authoritative-source import and identity-data validation
Orphan-account investigation and remediation results
Salesforce provisioning and reconciliation test evidence
Approval-routing test results
SAP SoD violations, mitigations, and exception ownership
Operational monitoring and failed-task escalation procedures
questions.explanation: The readiness package must connect source data, governance decisions, technical execution, remediation, exceptions, and operational support.

questions.prompt: Arrange the final go-live decision process.
choices: Validate the identity, account, and entitlement population
Confirm critical test scenarios and remediation results
Review unresolved high-risk defects and exceptions
Confirm monitoring, support ownership, and rollback procedures
Document residual risk and obtain accountable acceptance
Issue the go-live or delay recommendation
correctAnswers: Validate the identity, account, and entitlement population
Confirm critical test scenarios and remediation results
Review unresolved high-risk defects and exceptions
Confirm monitoring, support ownership, and rollback procedures
Document residual risk and obtain accountable acceptance
Issue the go-live or delay recommendation
questions.explanation: A defensible go-live decision requires reliable data, completed testing, risk review, operational readiness, explicit risk acceptance, and a documented recommendation.

questions.prompt: Which metrics should Northwind Bank monitor immediately after go-live?
choices: New orphan or incorrectly correlated accounts
Requests routed to fallback or incorrect approvers
